plan.confidence_note: The bot is up, but something above needs a look before I would call the steps certain.

sections.title: Right now
lines: Wave 1 (lowest rung only). Fight start estimate Sat 10/17 9:20 PM CT (in 2d 15h).
Moneyline right now: Blanchfield 76% to win, Jasudavicius 24%.
Sold 1,311 contracts so far; 2,108 more resting across 7 buckets. Premium $315.
Worst line -$285 (-$127 if every resting order filled). Backstop -$350; trickle target -$100 by the fight.
Wave 1 holds back 1,850 contracts of the ladder (only the lowest rung is posted) until Sat 10/17 9:00 AM CT (in 2d 2h).
The bot is running slow: it is set to check every 45s but its heartbeat only moves about every 1m. Slow reads and rate limits do this; timed steps can land a little late.

sections.title: Lagging sides
lines: Blanchfield by KO/TKO: sold 0, 600 behind the leader. Cheapest row 31c, fair 28.2c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 26.2c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 400 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.

Jasudavicius by KO/TKO: sold 0, 600 behind the leader. Cheapest row 9c, fair 7.9c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 5.9c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 250 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.

Jasudavicius by Decision: sold 188, 412 behind the leader. Cheapest row 15c, fair 12.4c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 10.4c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 400 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.

Blanchfield by Submission: sold 423, 177 behind the leader. Cheapest row 13c, fair 11.6c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 9.6c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 400 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.
The bot checks every 1m. The moneyline is rechecked every 5m (every 1m in the last 3 hours). Rows already resting are not repriced when the line moves; only new rows use the fresh fair.
A step is skipped if filling the new row in full would push the worst line lower.

sections.title: Next wave of contracts
lines: Wave 1 is posted: one lowest rung per bucket. At Sat 10/17 9:00 AM CT (in 2d 2h) the bot releases the rest of every ladder: 1,850 more contracts across 5 buckets.
Extra batches: a bucket whose resting falls under 25% of its allotment gets a batch of 50% of it (a third inside T-30), split 60/25/15 across three prices, up to 3 batches, 20 min apart, until T-3.
Blanchfield by Decision is thin (0 resting) but is 600 contracts ahead of the least-sold bucket (limit 300), so it gets no batch until the others catch up.
Closest to triggering: Jasudavicius by Submission with 140 resting against a trigger of 75.
The worst-line gate is closed: batches wait until the worst line is -$100 or better (it is -$285).
Batches used so far: 2.

sections.title: Tightening
lines: Trickle balancing starts at T-120 (Sat 10/17 7:20 PM CT, in 2d 13h): the bot records the worst line then and walks it to -$100 by the fight, selling small clips (50 contracts) at the bid, checking every 5 min, paying only when more than $25 behind, at most $100 paid per book.

From T-30: queue-preserving even-up (a bucket 15% behind the leader gets its lowest rung moved toward fair without losing queue). From T-5: a last-resort take is allowed; it is the old one-shot balancer and spends at most half the banked margin.
Between T-120 and T-30 the evenness allowance tightens on a time schedule, because a fight can end in seconds.
The fight start is an estimate from the card position on ESPN; if earlier bouts run long it moves, and every T- time here moves with it.

sections.title: Will it adapt on its own?
lines: Yes, on its own: the full ladder at the release time, extra batches on thin buckets while the gate is open, price steps on lagging buckets, and the paid trickle from T-120.
No, it will not: reprice resting rows when the moneyline moves, or add anything once the worst line is under the gate. The start time can shift if earlier bouts run long.
Depends on the crowd: the worst line is -$285 against a -$100 target. The trickle covers up to $100; the rest depends on fills on the lagging buckets.
I only read the bot's settings, state and log. I cannot see its next decision, only the rules it follows.
